question.text: The Musket Wars were a series of conflicts fought between the iwi, or tribes, of these Polynesian natives of New Zealand.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.leadin: Name the following World War II battles in the Pacific.
swap.text: Six months after Pearl Harbor, the U.S. sunk four of Japan's aircraft carriers during this battle, named after the atoll where it took place. The USS Yorktown was sunk during this battle.
swap.clue: The winning side in this battle lost the (+) Yorktown, whereas the losing side of this battle lost 4 aircraft carriers.

question.text: This British explorer and captain of the H.M.S. Endeavour was killed in Hawaii after attempting to kidnap Kamehameha's uncle Kalani'opu'u.
question.clue: The naturalists Daniel Solander and Joseph Banks accompanied this man on that voyage, during which this explorer visited Botany Bay.

swap.leadin: This island chain was discovered by Polynesian explorers from the Marquesas Islands using double-hulled canoes called "Waʻa."
swap.text: Name this island chain whose traditional mythology worshipped volcanoes such as Mauna Kea ["MOH-nuh KAY-uh"] and Kilauea ["key-loh-AY-uh"].
swap.clue: Locals call Las Vegas this chain's ninth island, and this group's Big Island is growing at 42 acres per year due to volcanic activity.

question.text: After Whitney's cotton gin patents proved unprofitable, Whitney worked with the US War Department to create these items with interchangeable parts.
question.clue: These weapons were brought to New Zealand by arriving merchants for trade, but unfortunately became used in intertribal conflict amongst the native Maori people. These items were first used for battle in Moremonui.

swap.text: This island chain is the last British holding in the Pacific Ocean. It is mainly inhabited by descendants of mutineers from the HMS Bounty.
swap.clue: Police officer Gail Cox denounced the culture of sexual abuse on this island, the subject of a controversial 2004 trial that convicted six of its residents.

question.leadin: The 1840 Constitution of this country was revised by the Great Mahele, which split its land in third between its monarchy, chiefs, and people.
question.text: Name this kingdom, whose "Law of the Splintered Paddle" guaranteed safe travel for women, children, and the elderly. This country was ruled for most of its existence by the Kamehameha dynasty.
question.clue: Its final ruler was forced to sign Lorrin Thurston's Bayonet Constitution, and this kingdom was succeeded by a republic led by Sanford Dole.

swap.leadin: This kingdom was annexed by the United States with the Newlands Resolution.
swap.text: Name this kingdom on whose namesake island James Cook was killed on his third voyage. This kingdom's'Iolani palace remains in modern Honolulu.

question.leadin: Answer the following about military engagements in the Philippines.
question.text: In October 1944, the Japanese fleet guarding the Philippines was destroyed here, allowing the U.S. to begin retaking the islands.
question.clue: Admiral Kurita withdrew from this battle which would be the last major action of the Japanese navy until Operation Ten-Go.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of Oceania.
swap.text: This nation in Oceania was the site of the Kokoda Track Campaign in World War II. It gained independence from Australia in 1975 and had to fend off a secessionist crisis on Bougainville Island.
swap.clue: This country is home to a dialect known as Unserdeutsch, or Rabaul Creole, reflecting its former status as Kaiser-Wilhelmsland during German colonization.

question.leadin: In the 1880s, this island was ruled by the English-Jewish-Tahitian merchant Alexander Salmon, who promoted the production of counterfeit rongorongo scripts.
question.text: Give the European name for this isolated Pacific island whose population was annihilated in the late 19th century. This island's huge moai statues are sometimes referred to as its namesake heads.
question.clue: This island's undeciphered rongorongo ("RON-go-RON-go") script has a glyph for the god Makemake ("MAH-kay-MAH-kay").

swap.leadin: The signing of this document is celebrated on a February 6 holiday.
swap.text: Name this 1840 treaty signed by British representatives and native chiefs, including Hone Heke and Te Wharerahi. It is considered the founding document of a modern day island nation.
swap.clue: James Prendergast termed this text a "simple nullity".

question.leadin: This country's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka was nicknamed "Colonel Steve Rambo" after his tendency to quote the Sylvester Stallone movie Rambo to describe a 1987 coup against Timoci Bavadra.
question.text: Name this country whose first indigenous prime minister Kamisese Mara attempted to seize power from Mahendra Chaudhry, who descended from the girmityas, during a coup led by George Speight in 2000.
question.answerHtml: Fiji [or Republic of Fiji; or Matanitu Tugalala o Viti]
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.leadin: Robert Louis Stevenson's book A Footnote to History describes how a diplomatic standoff in this country was averted when a cyclone wrecked all the warships in its harbor.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country whose independence was advocated for by the Mau movement. Germany was granted administration of this island country in 1899, while the US administered a set of islands to the east.
swap.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

question.leadin: This ruler won a battle that was so violent that it became known as the "damming of the waters" due to the corpses blocking the flow of the 'Iao ("EE-ow").
question.text: Name ruler who won a decisive victory at Kepaniwai with the help of Welsh cannoneer Isaac Davis. This ruler hired Australian convicts Mela and Black Jack to design the Brick Palace for his favorite queen, Ka'ahumanu ("kuh-AH-hoo-MAH-noo").
question.clue: This ruler who established the Law of the Splintered Paddle after winning battles at Kawela and the Pali Lookout.

swap.text: The Samoan independence movement was named after this native word, roughly translated as "resolute testimony." An earlier movement named after this word was led by the Pule ("poo-LAY") chief Lauaki Mamoe ("lao-AH-kee muh-MOH-ee").
swap.answerHtml: Mau [accept Mau Movement; accept Mau a Pule; accept O le Mau; reject “Mau Mau”]

question.leadin: The "entangled bank hypothesis" of this process uses Y-chromosomal DNA to argue against a rapid origin from Asia and suggest that it was driven by millenia of cultural mixing.
question.text: Identify this long-term historical process. Jared Diamond wrote an article likening the Lapita culture to an "express train" that kicked off this process. A description is fine.
question.answerHtml: Polynesian expansion [or Polynesian migration; accept answers indicating the movement of Polynesian peoples or Polynesians or Austronesians across the Pacific/Oceania; prompt on answers referring to settling any of the Pacific, or Oceania, or Polynesia]

swap.leadin: In 1869, the HMS Rosario seized and freed victims of this practice aboard the Daphne.
swap.text: Name this practice of kidnapping Pacific Islanders to work on Australian plantations. In 2021, Bundaberg's mayor Jack Dempsey formally apologized for this practice, which may have affected over 100,000 people.
swap.clue: Louis Becke fictionalized his travels with Bully Hayes while he was engaging in this practice.

question.text: In spite of being ostensibly committed to socialism as a member of the Labour Party, this finance minister implemented a series of supply-side reforms in the 1980s to try to restart New Zealand's stagnant economy.

swap.leadin: The Samoan government cancelled Christmas ceremonies in 2019 due to one of these events.
swap.text: Identify this type of event that killed over 80 Samoans in part due to conspiracy theories popularized by Edwin Tamasese.
swap.answerHtml: measles outbreak [prompt on outbreak or epidemic or diseases or similar answers]
